Subject: Recap + next steps: private/on-prem requirements and maintenance windows

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and asks so we can scope a Private (air-gapped) deployment and draft an SOW: 

1) Deployment mode you prefer: Private VPC on-prem (air-gapped) — you confirmed this is the direction, correct?
2) Hardware baseline: you mentioned Dell R750s with A100 nodes — can you confirm GPU counts per rack and whether you anticipate rolling hardware refreshes vs full cluster replacements?
3) Offline maintenance: please confirm typical weekly backup windows and any blackout windows where maintenance cannot occur.
4) Upgrades cadence: how often do you want Redwood to push firmware/OS/model runtime upgrades (monthly/quarterly/biannual)? We need this to define offline upgrade playbook.
5) Security/KMS: confirm whether you will provide an on-prem HSM or just an internal KMS (we support both, but implementation differs).

Next steps we propose: 1) internal tech call (Markus) to align on maintenance playbook and upgrade approach; 2) Redwood to share an initial offline maintenance playbook and SOW draft; 3) schedule a 30-min follow-up to pick a pilot maintenance window.

Attaching the initial mutual-action plan spreadsheet I referenced.

Attachment: initial_ma_plan.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

If the above looks right, can you confirm hardware details and preferred maintenance windows?

Thanks,

From: Daniel Rivera <daniel.rivera@acme-bio.com>

Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: private/on-prem requirements and maintenance windows

Neha — thanks for the clear recap. A few responses inline: 

1) Yes, Private VPC on-prem (air-gapped) is the path we prefer.
2) Hardware: we currently have 6 Racks, each populated with Dell R750 chassis. Typical node spec is 4x A100 80GB per server; roughly 2 servers per rack dedicated for inference (12 servers total initially). We expect a rolling refresh once per year (replace older servers in waves).
3) Offline maintenance: we run an overnight weekly backup every Sunday 01:00–04:00 local. Any maintenance requiring network egress must be scheduled outside that window. Blackout: no maintenance Tue/Wed 08:00–18:00 local due to release cycles.
4) Upgrades: we prefer a conservative cadence — minor patches monthly, major upgrades (runtime/kernel changes) biannually.
5) HSM/KMS: we will not provide an HSM at pilot; we have an internal KMS backed by our key-management services.

Forwarding the network topology diagram for context.

Attachment: network_topo.png (image/png)

Happy to join Markus for the tech alignment call later today if that works.

—Daniel

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: private/on-prem requirements and maintenance windows

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the details, that's very helpful. A few notes from the infra/solutions side and an attached starter playbook: 

- Rolling refresh once per year: we will design the cluster to tolerate N-2 server loss during refresh; propose staging nodes and can run canary inference traffic to validate before cutover.
- Weekly offline backup window (Sun 01:00–04:00): we recommend Redwood scheduled maintenance align with that window for non-disruptive KV cache snapshots and database flushes. For kernel/runtime upgrades that require an offline period, we recommend a 02:00–04:00 window on Sundays to minimize overlap with your release blackout.
- Upgrade cadence: we can separate patches (hotfixes) that are non-invasive vs full runtime/model updates that require an offline maintenance window. For major upgrades, we'll provide a targeted rollback plan and snapshotting guidance.
- KMS: since an HSM is not available at pilot, we'll integrate with your KMS using our customer-managed keyflow (bring-your-own-keys pattern). If you later adopt an HSM, we can swap to an HSM-backed flow with minimal downtime.

Operational specifics we want to capture in the playbook: pre-maintenance checklist (backups, KV cache persistence, node cordon), maintenance actions (drain, apply firmware/runtime, model rewarm), post-maintenance validation (latency smoke tests, sample queries, log sampling), and emergency rollback steps.

I attached a first-pass "Redwood offline maintenance playbook" (v1) that maps these steps to roles, estimated durations, and test criteria. If that looks OK, we'll turn it into a SOW appendix.

Attachment: redwood-offline-playbook-v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Proposed next step: 30-min tech alignment tomorrow 10:00 AM ET (we'll bring an SRE + infra engineer). Neha, can you confirm and create the invite? Daniel, does that time work for you?

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
